definition: Capacious means roomy enough to hold or contain a very great deal, with plenty of open space inside.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word capacious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know capacious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The old theater's capacious lobby swallowed the entire crowd without ever feeling full, its marble floor stretching well past the last row of coat racks.
Snug sits at the small end of the scale: a snug reading nook fits one person cozily, while a capacious library hall could take in hundreds of readers and all their books.
A roomy apartment gives you comfortable space to live in, but a capacious warehouse loft goes further — it could swallow the furniture of three apartments and still feel open.

Spacious means offering plenty of open room and stresses an open, airy feel. Capacious is more specific: it measures how much something can hold or take in, so a capacious bag may not look spacious at all from the outside.

Commodious means roomy in a comfortable, convenient way — a commodious cabin is pleasant to settle into. Capacious says nothing about comfort; it stresses pure holding power, the sheer amount that fits inside.

Voluminous describes something bulky and large in outward volume, like a voluminous cloak that spreads wide around the wearer. Capacious looks inward instead, at the room something offers for holding things — a case can be slim outside yet capacious within.
Uncomfortably small, with too little room to hold or move — the direct opposite of capacious, which describes generous interior space that holds a great deal.
Restricted to a tight, closed-in space with no room to spare — the reverse of the open, take-anything-in roominess that capacious describes.
The rangers set a humane trap to capture the escaped parrot before nightfall.
Capacious means roomy enough to hold or contain a very great deal, with plenty of open space inside.
The walk-in closet was so capacious that it held her entire wardrobe, three suitcases, and a full-length mirror, with room left over to stand and dress comfortably in the middle.
Capacious means having a large interior space able to hold a great deal.
It's not just big on the outside (a solid boulder can be huge yet hold nothing); it's specifically about how much open room there is inside to contain things.
The closet swallowing a whole wardrobe plus suitcases and still leaving space to move is exactly what capacious describes.
Capacious is a formal, somewhat literary word, at home in descriptive writing about buildings, vehicles, containers, and even the mind ('a capacious memory').
In everyday speech, say 'roomy' or 'big inside,' but reach for capacious when you want to emphasize that something holds an impressively great deal.

The county's first bookmobile was a converted bread van, and the librarian who drove it judged it by a single measure.
Not speed, not looks: capacity.
The van was surprisingly capacious, taking in twelve hundred volumes once shelvers learned to use every hollow behind the wheel wells.
Visitors were always startled.
From the outside it seemed too small for a tenth of that, squat and plain in the school parking lot.
